title: <sup>11</sup>C-Labeling of acyclic retinoid peretinoin by rapid C-[<sup>11</sup>C]methylation to disclose novel brain permeability and central nervous system activities hidden in antitumor agent.
abstract: Recently, retinoid actions on the central nervous system (CNS) have attracted considerable attention from the perspectives of brain disease diagnosis and drug development. Firstly, we successfully synthesized [<sup>11</sup>C]peretinoin esters (methyl, ethyl, and benzyl) using a Pd(0)-mediated rapid C-[<sup>11</sup>C]methylation of the corresponding stannyl precursors without geometrical isomerization in 82%, 66%, and 57% radiochemical yields (RCYs). Subsequent hydrolysis of the <sup>11</sup>C-labeled ester produced [<sup>11</sup>C]peretinoin in 13 ± 8% RCY (n = 3). After pharmaceutical formulation, the resulting [<sup>11</sup>C]benzyl ester and [<sup>11</sup>C]peretinoin had high radiochemical purity (>99% each) and molar activities of 144 and 118 ± 49 GBq μmol<sup>-1</sup> at total synthesis times of 31 min and 40 ± 3 min, respectively. Rat brain PET imaging for the [<sup>11</sup>C]ester revealed a unique time-radioactivity curve, suggesting the participation of the acid [<sup>11</sup>C]peretinoin for the brain permeability. However, the curve of the [<sup>11</sup>C]peretinoin rose steadily after a shorter time lag to reach 1.4 standardized uptake value (SUV) at 60 min. These various phenomena between the ester and acid became more pronounced in the monkey brain (SUV of > 3.0 at 90 min). With the opportunity to identify high brain uptake of [<sup>11</sup>C]peretinoin, we discovered CNS activities of a drug candidate called peretinoin, such as the induction of a stem-cell to neuronal cell differentiation and the suppression of neuronal damages.
